note: Stage one, the gate on draft 3. 9:19 ('para sempre') passes. Four verses: 9:6 minor (third time, refused), 9:10 MAJOR (second time, held), 9:12 minor (taken: 'feitos'), 9:13 MAJOR — new, on words he passed on drafts 1 and 2 — held. So stage one closes with two majors standing against the gate, both on unchanged words that an earlier reading of his had passed or marked minor; both are logged here and in the report.

outcomes.remark: 'pelos séculos dos séculos' → 'pelo século do século' (minor, third time)

outcomes.reason: Held on purpose, as at 118:114 (D24): the glossary row adjútor → auxílio; the metonymy of suscéptor → amparo.

outcomes.remark: stúdia names activities (the Greek ἐπιτηδεύματα) rather than intentions → 'os seus feitos' (minor)
outcomes.reason: Right on the Greek, and the blind reader had not known 'desígnios'; 'feitos' serves 13:1b too.

outcomes.remark: eórum completes recordátus est ('he remembered them'); the translation ties it only to the blood (MAJOR) → 'ao pedir contas do sangue, ele se lembrou deles'
outcomes.reason: Held on purpose. The parse is possible Latin, but the Gallican is here the Greek word for word (ἐκζητῶν τὰ αἵματα αὐτῶν ἐμνήσθη: the pronoun is the blood's, the verb has no object), and he had passed these exact words twice. The unexpressed object of 'se lembrou' keeps open whom he remembered, which the blind reader heard as the poor. His fix and Douay-Rheims' doubled pronoun ('do sangue deles, ele se lembrou deles') are options 2 and 3.

note: Stage one, draft 4 (revise_v4.py; draft 3 kept): 9:12 'os seus feitos' (Latinist, minor). 9:13 unchanged in the text; the slot v13rec was added so that the Latinist's and Douay-Rheims' readings can be selected. Not re-read by a critic: a one-word change proposed by the gate itself. Stage one ends here, at 9:21 (the end of Hebrew Ps 9).
